newsitem.title: UK: UK natural gas steadies, September bounces back.
newsitem.headline: UK natural gas steadies, September bounces back.

text.p: U.K. natural gas spot prices were mostly steady on Thursday, although the front full month September, the market leader in the past few days, bounced back from Wednesday's losses.

September was actively traded on the IPE, and higher numbers gave a boost to prices on the OTC market and helped the contract break back through the psychologically important nine pence a therm level to trade at a high of 9.05 pence.

Some players noted that on some days traders were using futures to swing sentiment on the spot market. Thursday saw a brisk day of trade on the IPE with 540 lots changing hands, helping to push open interest over 6000 lots, or six million therms a day.
"When the screen is liquid people are realising they can use it to lead the market," said one trader.
Prompt gas was also firm, with within day and day ahead deals done at or above nine pence.
But the rest of the curve failed to recover any of Wednesday's losses.
The fourth quarter traded at 13 pence, the lower end of Wednesday's range, while the first quarter next year was steady at 16.85 pence.
"Earlier in the week I think people weren't happy with the premium for winter over summer gas, but it seems to be quite settled at this level," a dealer said.
Next summer edged higher to trade at 10.80 pence, while the fourth quarter next year held in contango against the equivalent quarter this year, trading at 13.45 pence.
